completedSteps.name: Task 7.1 - Implement tests/parity/parity_runner.py
completedSteps.notes: 717 lines. ComparisonMode enum (EXACT, SET_EQUALITY, TOLERANCE). DEFAULT_TOLERANCE=0.10 matching the design's 'scores within 10%' requirement. ParityResult + ParitySummary + ParityCase dataclasses. ToolCaller = Callable[[str, dict], Awaitable[Any]] protocol — the framework is transport-agnostic so tests inject mocks and production can inject HTTPJSONRPCToolCaller (Streamable-HTTP MCP client via httpx, lazy-imported). ParityRunner.assert_parity dispatches both calls concurrently via asyncio.gather (worst-case latency max(node, python), not sum). Comparison algorithms: _compare_exact (deep equals, reports full values on diff), _compare_sets (Counter-based multiset so ['foo','foo'] != ['foo']; reports missing_in_python / extra_in_python deltas), _compare_tolerance (element-wise relative delta |x-y| / max(|x|,|y|,1) with near-zero guard, surfaces max_relative_delta in ParityResult.extra). Extractor hooks (id_extractor, name_extractor, score_extractor) let each tool project its own response to the comparable subset. run_cases() batches with --module filter for per-module parity testing. CLI: --nodejs-url, --python-url (default :3000/:8000), --module, --cases-file, --tolerance, --nodejs-header/--python-header (AgentCore bearer-token support via repeatable KEY=VALUE). Framework makes zero live calls by itself.

completedSteps.name: Task 17.1 - Implement src/tools/utility.py (4 tools)
completedSteps.notes: 1010 lines. register(mcp, data, *, state_dir=None, server_version=None) registers 4 tools on the FastMCP instance. Input schemas match Node.js UnifiedMCPServer.js exactly: get_server_info(include_capabilities: bool=False); mcp_health_check(detailed: bool=False, deep: bool=False, functional: bool=False); get_health_trend(limit: int=10); get_quality_metrics(category: Literal['code_structure','semantic_search','architecture','ee2_compliance','operational','cross_language']|None=None, compare: bool=False). All tools return markdown (matches Node.js text-content format). get_server_info: uses mcp.list_tools() for live tool count, _infer_active_modules() maps current tool names back to the 9 canonical modules, version from src.mcp_server.SERVER_VERSION (lazy import avoids circular deps). mcp_health_check: awaits data.health_check(deep=...) when data is not None; degrades cleanly to 'disabled' row when data is None (first-deploy smoke-test scenario); deep=True persists snapshot to state_dir/health_history.jsonl in the Node.js-compatible schema {timestamp, source, neo4j:{status,nodes,relationships,latency_ms}, chromadb:{status,collections,total_docs,latency_ms}, drift:{neo4j_node_delta, chromadb_doc_delta}} with drift computed against last prior snapshot. get_health_trend: reads state_dir/health_history.jsonl, tails last N, renders count/latency trend table + >10% consecutive-change anomaly detection. get_quality_metrics: reads state_dir/quality_metrics.jsonl (one snapshot per line), formats Overall + per-Category tables + optional regression comparison against prior snapshot with [IMPROVED]/[DEGRADED] tags (lower-is-better for latency_* metrics). State dir resolution precedence: explicit arg -> SDD_STATE_DIR env -> 'sdd_framework/execution_state' default.

get_quality_metrics reads state_dir/quality_metrics.jsonl per the user's instruction. The Node.js original reads from mcp_server_node/test/benchmark/results/*.json (one JSON file per run). The Python format is a single JSONL file, one snapshot per line. If true parity with Node.js is needed in Phase B4 parity tests for this tool, either change the Python format or write a compatibility shim that consolidates the directory of JSONs into a JSONL.

The ParityRunner's HTTPJSONRPCToolCaller targets Streamable-HTTP. If the production AgentCore proxy uses the /invocations-style endpoint via bedrock-agentcore-control, tests will need to supply a custom ToolCaller that delegates to agentcore-kiro-proxy.py, as the framework supports.
